title: Aurum Alpha browser bootstrap document
description: What the origin that served the bundle tells the client, rendered from THAT origin's environment and served at /config.json with Cache-Control: no-store. Governed by standards/090-web-client.md WC2. Deliberately minimal: it exists to solve the ordering problem that the client cannot ask the API where the API is, and to tell a bundle which environment and which estate surface it landed on. Everything the backend knows about itself belongs on GET /api/config, and the frontend's own build provenance is compiled into the bundle. Served to every anonymous visitor and therefore PUBLIC BY CONSTRUCTION. schemaVersion 3 - see the schema_version note.

schema_version.description: Version 1 carried a 'build' object; version 2 removed it because build provenance is compiled in. Version 3 renames every field for what it is (api_origin was api_base_url and was always an origin; login_path and logout_path leave the 'auth' wrapper, which named nothing; global_flags was 'features' and was always the anonymous global subset of 038 FF7), adds surface_class so one contract serves the front door, the product and internal tools (standards/091-web-estate.md WE1), and adds surface_settings for the per-surface, per-environment values a front door needs. A rename is breaking under PC6 and so takes a new version; the deprecation window is nil because no implementation consumed version 2 - stated rather than assumed.

environment.description: Which environment served this bundle. The bundle is identical across all of them (WC2); this is how the running client knows where it landed, and how a development deploy of a front door is stopped from pointing at a production booking link.

surface_class.description: Which estate surface this document serves (091 WE1). A front door has no session and no API, so api_origin, login_path and logout_path are absent for it; a product or internal surface requires all three. The conditional below holds that.

api_origin.description: The origin the API client (WC3) calls: scheme, host and port, no path. Under WC1 the browser sends a session cookie and no Authorization header, so this is an origin that cookie is scoped to and no cross-origin credential handling arises. Named for what it is; the earlier name said url and the description said origin.

login_path.description: The path the client navigates to in order to begin a session. A top-level navigation, not a fetch - the OIDC provider must be able to render its own UI and redirect back. Under WC1 the browser's behaviour is identical whichever authentication architecture is in place, so it is told where to navigate and nothing about the architecture, which belongs to standards/060-auth.md.

logout_path.description: The path that ends the session. Ending it is the server's job, not the page's: the session's real state lives server-side and the browser cannot revoke it by discarding anything it holds (WC1).

global_flags.description: The anonymous, global subset of the evaluated flag set of standards/038-feature-flags.md FF7: flag name to boolean, for flags declared served_to_client with global scope. Present so that a toggle is never a reason to rebuild the bundle, which is the WC2 failure this document exists to prevent. Tenant- and user-scoped flags arrive in the authenticated application configuration, never here, because this document is served before anyone is known.

surface_settings.description: Configuration specific to this surface, rendered from the serving origin's environment: a booking link, a form endpoint, a status page. Keys are snake_case and are DECLARED PER REPOSITORY in a schema that repository's CI validates the served document against, so an undeclared key is a finding there; this shared contract holds only the shape. Values are scalars: a nested object here is application configuration wearing a bootstrap's name, and belongs on /api/config. Nothing secret, because this document is public (WC2).
